The least obvious thing to do when things are going well is to stop. But that's exactly what we did last week Stairpay.

Over the last 12 months we have reached 75,000 Shared Ownership homes on the platform
and tripled our ARR while keeping headcount the same. ?

On paper, that's amazing, but we felt it was necessary to pause for a couple of days and all align on what success looks like in 12 months, 24 months and longer term. 

Our mission has been the same since day 1, increase the supply of affordable homes. We do that by increasing transparency into affordable housing and improving operational efficiency. ?

To date we have helped thousands of people achieve full homeownership, but we're still far from making a dent in the housing crisis. 

If we tripled our number of homes again within #SharedOwnership we'd have 100% of the SO market, so it's no surprise we're going to expand both our product range within shared ownership, and outside.

Our first session revolved around: what must be true by September 2027 for us to hit our company targets. 

Here's what we came up with:

1. Stairpay is the first port of call for Shared Owners
2. Stairpay holds synoptic data on housing (ask Daniel Larbi if you've not heard that word before ?)
3. There are 5,000 non Shared Ownership homes on Stairpay across multiple landlords
4. All employees understand each other's weekly workload, priorities and delivery timelines
5. If Stairpay was down for 15 minutes all of our clients would notice

The bar has been raised for the next year, and I cannot be more excited about it!

?? How much longer can your organisation live with messy siloed data? 

My entire LinkedIn feed is peppered with posts on AI, so here's my take. 

? AI can't help you if it can't fetch the right information. Start with cleaning your data or you're wasting your money.

Here's what we hear a lot:

"I've submitted a ticket to get rental information from IT"

"We've been through a few mergers so we can't access that information"

"I need to check Dynamics and the sales CRM as they don't match"

"Can you integrate with (_insert software name built in the 1980s_)"

? Based on what I've seen from the organisations I've spoken to in the sector there is very little point in investing heavily in AI that touches operational staff until you sort out the data first.

Call me sad but this email received from one of our clients about our new Compliance module genuinely brought a tear to my eye. 

There is so much work that goes on behind the scenes when building a tech product, in order to make it useful, but also simple to use.

This particular email was off the back of an intense few weeks for Daniel Larbi, Tim Otto and the rest of the team at Stairpay to get our Compliance module v1 shipped.

One thing I expect we?ll get asked a lot over the coming months is:

?What makes Stairpay lease extraction different from just using ChatGPT / Claude / Copilot??

Fair question. ?

If all you want is to upload a lease and get back a summary, general-purpose AI can already do a decent job of that (although some of the hand written leases we?ve seen would definitely test it).

But that?s not the real problem housing associations are trying to solve.

The real problem is teams spending hours:

???? Checking leases manually
? Pulling out key details
? Re-reading the same documents every time a new case, question, or exception comes up

So for me, the real unlock isn?t AI that reads a lease.

It?s what happens next. ??

Can the information be structured properly?

Can someone ask a plain-English question and get an answer they can trust?

Can that answer link back to the lease itself?

Can the right information appear inside the workflows teams already use, instead of sitting in another tab that gets opened once and forgotten?

That?s what we?re focused on. ?

Not just scanning documents.

Reading them once. Extracting what matters. Then making that information usable across the platform.

So instead of re-reading the same lease for every resale, staircasing case, resident query, or edge case?

Teams upload it once. Scan it once. And get the answers they need, when and where they need them.

That feels much closer to the real opportunity.

Not AI as a demo. AI as infrastructure. ?

Big milestone for us at Stairpay ?

Today we?re launching our new website ? and for the first time publicly sharing where we?re heading over the next few years.

When I started Stairpay 4 years ago, the vision was:

Build the digital infrastructure affordable homeownership has never had.

At the beginning, that sounded exciting.

Then reality hit.

If you try to solve too many problems for too many people, you end up solving none.

So we made a strategic decision to focus on one thing:

Staircasing ?

We changed our name from Pluto to Stairpay and doubled down on building the best staircasing platform in the market.

4 years later, 1 in 3 Shared Ownership homes are on the platform.

Something I?m incredibly proud of ? although I didn?t expect us to become known as ?the staircasing guys? ?

But working closely with Housing Associations taught us something important:

Teams don?t just need point solutions.

They need better infrastructure.

The right information, in the right place, at the right time.

That?s what we?ve been building toward.

So alongside the new website, we?re launching several new modules:

- Listings ? fill homes faster with less admin ?
- Compliance ? pass audits without the fire drill ?
- Resident Portal ? reduce resident queries and capture cleaner data ?
- Comms ? reach the right residents and prove every message ?
- Finance ? understand residents and de-risk portfolios ?

Together, these modules create an operating system for #SharedOwnership:

One platform connecting Housing Association workflows directly with residents.

Not disparate workflows stitched together through a generalist CRM ? but purpose-built infrastructure designed alongside some of the largest Shared Ownership providers in the UK.

There?s a lot more coming.

If you want to see where we?re headed, check out the new website ?

The most important part of being a software business is staying close to customers and constantly trying to understand their pain points.

Yesterday, we cohosted a tech roundtable with the nsg to talk about what the most common problems are with Sales, Staircasing, Resales and Leasehold Management in #SharedOwnership.

And given it's everywhere now, we focused heavily on #AI. 

When thinking about AI adoption, many Housing Associations are very in favour, but scared at the same time. 

? What if AI gets things wrong? What if it makes things up?

My response? 

????? Get AI to do what you would otherwise get an army of 100 interns to do, not the high stakes tasks. Then you check the most important parts.

Closing a sale on the phone? Human job

Scanning tens of thousands of leases to extract rent indexation? AI's job.

Stairpay isn't here to take anyone's job away, we exist to remove the low value repetitive tasks, so that you can focus on making residents happier.

Want to chat to me about how we can scan tens of thousands of leases and help you make more sense of your data? Get in touch!

Here's a preview of what's to come:

2026, let's go! ??

A little pinch me moment ??

A year ago we were a SaaS business with ?0 MRR, a few pilots under our belt and a lot of frustration as to why we couldn't get people to fully adopt our solution. 

Today I can say that there are around 250,000 #sharedownership properties in the UK and as of the start of the new financial year 1 in 3 will be on Stairpay.

At no point did I stop believing, at no point did I think about quitting, but I must admit it was a monumental task to get to where we are today, so I'm knackered.

All founders are terrible at celebrating successes, including me, so here's me trying:

? Getting to ?10k MRR was the single hardest thing I've ever done in my career. It took over 3 years. Getting to ?20k MRR took one month. I closed every one of those contracts.

?? Getting 30% market share in 12 months in a market that is notoriously impenetrable is not something that anyone can do. So clearly the team built something people value.

????? At no point have there been more than 7 of us in the team, which means we're all exhausted, but we're also more excited than ever to come back for more.

? We have bootstrapped the whole year. No pointless metrics, no silly marketing spend, no pleasing anyone, apart from our customers.

--- ?? If I fast forward one more year, what would success look like? ---

? I want at least 50% of Shared Ownership properties on Stairpay. We already have nearly half G15 on board, so this will require working with many more smaller RPs.

? I want to help people get into Shared Ownership and progress through it with ease. I want every Shared Owner to know who we are, and be able to support them.

? I want us to be the de-facto operating system for Shared Ownership. Sales, Marketing, Homeownership, Rent, Service Charge, Staircasing and Resales, all in one place.

? I want to build the first open database for Shared Ownership. Not a one-off data exercise. A live platform anyone can query to speak facts, not opinions on the tenure.

Thank you to everyone who has placed their trust in us and in me. As I said above, I am in dire need of some R&R so I'll be taking a couple of weeks off to spend it with the two most precious people in my life. Emilia is still a terrible sleeper, so probably won't rest, but I'll definitely recharge!

See you in 2026 ??

Proud moment alert ?

I started Stairpay in April 2022, and on day 1 it was just me in a coffee shop across the road from my flat. 

Every working day for 9 months, I'd go in there with my laptop for the whole day, ordering a drink every two hours to avoid getting kicked out.

In December 2022 we raised some money, so I upgraded to getting a hot-desking pass with WeWork. I decided not to get an office until we could afford it out of our own pocket, not investor money.

Every working day since then, the team and I have been lugging a backpack back and forth to different WeWorks in London, trying to get there early enough to sit together.

In the last month we've nearly doubled the team, making it pretty difficult to take over the co-working desks at the WeWork, so I knew the time had come.

I'm excited to share that in two weeks, Stairpay will have their first proper office. 

Not gonna lie, seeing our name on the lift made me choke up a bit, not because of the achievement, but the way we got there. 

This is not me spending VC money on some fancy office we can't afford, this is hard earned cash from the huge amount of work we put in for the last 3 years.

I really look forward to the next chapter! ?
